# SPD-086 — Edit hook: a deliverable glob naming a Next.js dynamic segment ([email]) is read as a character class, so it matches nothing

## Brief
Filed by [[BADS-054/Snowden]] (02, reviewer) while reviewing BAD-054 PR 1, as proposal 95+9; recorded here rather than as a BadTakes ticket because the fix is in this repository.

`hooks/pathrule.glob_to_regex` reads `[` as the start of a character class, exactly as a shell glob does. A deliverable naming a Next.js dynamic route segment therefore matches no real path: `admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/**` compiles to a class over `e`, `m`, `a`, `i`, `l`, so the only paths it can match are ones with a single letter where the directory name belongs.

The effect is that an agent is silently **read-only on the exact files it owns**. Snowden was refused `admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/page.tsx` — "Law 5: … is not among BADS-054/Snowden's deliverables (admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/**)" — quoting its own planned glob back at it. It worked around this by doing every fault injection in rsync copies outside the checkout, so BAD-054's review still happened, but a reviewer told to fix a defect in place could not have.

Reproduced directly:

```python
from spudlib.hooks.pathrule import path_matches_glob as m
p = 'admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/_components/UserTab.tsx'
m(p, 'admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/**')   # False
m(p, 'admin/src/app/accounts/?email?/**')   # True
m(p, 'admin/src/app/accounts/**')           # True
```

Two candidate fixes, and the choice is the work:

1. **Escape the metacharacters** when a deliverable names a literal bracket. Note that the obvious shell spelling `[[]email[]]` does **not** survive `glob_to_regex` either: the `[]]` branch finds its closing `]` at the first character, emits an empty class, and the regex that comes out is malformed rather than literal. So an escape needs its own handling, not just documentation.
2. **Match as a literal prefix** when a glob has no wildcard outside a trailing `/**`. Narrower in effect and it costs the caller nothing, but it changes the meaning of a glob that deliberately uses a class.

Whichever is chosen, `member new` should refuse — or at least warn about — a deliverable glob that can match no path under the project, since the current failure is silent until an agent is mid-run and blames its own brief. That refusal is worth more than the escape.

Pin it with a test that plans a deliverable naming a `[segment]` directory and asserts a write inside it is allowed, and with the three `path_matches_glob` cases above.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus in a worktree: the change is a few lines in glob_to_regex plus the tests that pin it. A reviewer is unnecessary; the test suite is the proof.
